mbm-2726.clue: Lane seven keeps my pencil upright.
mbm-2726.quote: When I finally made that stubborn corner spare, my aunt stood my pencil in the finger hole of my bowling ball like a flagpole. We left its little paper flag waving till my next turn.

mbm-2727.clue: I can pull a cloud from a teacup.
mbm-2727.quote: I fold a white paper napkin and tuck it under the saucer before I pour. When the steam rises, a tug makes a paper cloud open above the cup. My nephew brings his toy plane for the encore.

mbm-2728.clue: We cross the sea with one bent penny.
mbm-2728.quote: I made a board game from an old road atlas. A bent penny stands upright like a sail to carry players across the printed water. We always argue over who gets to be the ferry captain.

mbm-2729.quote: At the ceramics museum I look for mended bowls. I drew one crack in my notebook and found a whole river delta in it. The perfect bowls will have to wait for my next visit.

mbm-2730.clue: That green hat belongs to the mayor.
mbm-2730.quote: Our game lost its mayor piece, so we elected a sugar cube. It lasted one cup of tea. Now a green wooden fellow in a top hat wears a paper sash, and we hold the elections after dessert.

mbm-2731.clue: My first square has a door in it.
mbm-2731.quote: I dropped a stitch right in the middle of a crochet blanket. My niece slipped her finger through and pretended to knock. I made a tiny curtain for the hole.

mbm-2732.clue: I made a plate the size of an apology.
mbm-2732.quote: I broke my brother's smallest saucer years ago. On my first pottery course I made him one so big the cup looks like a pond with an island. He uses it for breakfast and an entire slice of toast.

mbm-2733.clue: At high tide I visit the same fence post.
mbm-2733.quote: A weathered post sticks up behind the harbor reeds. When I pull up in my kayak, the shell line on it is a neat little ruler. My pencil marks show how the water met me each Sunday.

mbm-2734.clue: My bookshelf has a quiet seat at the end.
mbm-2734.quote: I built one low shelf in the window and put a cushion beside it. Friends visit for a book recommendation and disappear there for an hour. That's my favorite review.

mbm-2735.clue: I can tell the time by a patch of shade.
mbm-2735.quote: I spread my towel where I can watch the leaves throw shadows across the courtyard tiles. I’m allowed one tile’s worth of daydreaming before I go back in and turn the peaches.

mbm-2736.clue: I go back for the empty frame.
mbm-2736.quote: A museum lent out its biggest landscape and put a small sketch in that huge frame. I loved having to step close to find it. I drew my whole visit in one square inch of my notebook.

mbm-2737.clue: The kite tail was my hardest seam.
mbm-2737.quote: I stitched a kite on our spring quilt and gave it a tail of old shoelaces. My daughter learned to tie bows on that blanket. Some of the neatest ribbons are hers.

mbm-2738.clue: I only race the postbox at the corner.
mbm-2738.quote: On my morning run I can see the red mail van round the far corner. Some days I reach the postbox first. The driver opens the box with a little bow whenever I win.

mbm-2739.clue: I keep the flour on my fingers.
mbm-2739.quote: I marked the quilt pattern in flour before my first sewing class. Mum had drawn her recipe in little pictures on the sack I cut up for the back. We baked from it once before I stitched it shut.

mbm-2740.quote: At the corn contest my winning cob still had one kernel tucked away at the end. I saved it in a matchbox, planted it and got one stubborn little stalk. My nephew calls it the champion returning.

mbm-2741.clue: The last tune came home in a pie dish.
mbm-2741.quote: After our session I was still tapping a reel on the table. The man who'd brought the apple pie turned her empty dish over and taught me the rhythm I'd missed, using two spoons. I washed up for him while the tune was still in my wrists.

mbm-2742.clue: There are four corners and five of us.
mbm-2742.quote: I quilted a blanket for our family's five chairs. Everyone wanted a corner, so I added a small triangle sticking out along one edge. The littlest chair gets the pointiest corner.

mbm-2743.clue: My list has a square cut out of it.
mbm-2743.quote: I carried a scrap of blue tile to the market to match a chipped one at home. A stallholder found its twin in a tray of buttons. It's a button in the wall now, and nobody guesses which.

mbm-2744.clue: I can hit the moon from our yard.
mbm-2744.quote: When the full moon hangs just above our hedge my friend photographs my frisbee crossing it. It took forty throws to get the picture. The neighbor's dog came over for every single attempt.

mbm-2745.clue: The camp mugs all point east.
mbm-2745.quote: Before bed I stack our tin cups with the handles facing sunrise. First person up slips hot cocoa into the top one. My cousin caught me setting an alarm to get that job.

mbm-2746.clue: I make the knot travel uphill.
mbm-2746.quote: I tie a loose knot in a bright yellow rope and slide it to the end without touching the middle. My friend listens for the swish when it moves. He says a good trick should have a soundtrack.

mbm-2747.clue: My first passenger was a paper clip.
mbm-2747.quote: I made a little timetable for the freight trains outside my school. Dad bent a paper clip into a passenger and set it on top of my notebook. We both know freight trains don't take him. He comes anyway.

mbm-2748.clue: I count lanes with my fingertips.
mbm-2748.quote: After the early swim I can feel the tiled lines of the pool beside my fingertips long after I've dried off. I draw one blue stripe along the edge of my calendar for every morning I make it.

mbm-2749.clue: The boat in my painting is made of shadows.
mbm-2749.quote: I painted a little boat in our harbor and left room for a sail. My sister held a leaf between the paper and the sun, and a perfect sail appeared. We waited till the wind drew a whole fleet.

mbm-2750.clue: I like the first ripple best.
mbm-2750.quote: Our town pool opens before the bakery. I sit at the edge and watch one ripple reach the little clock at the far end. Once it's touched the opposite wall I can start my laps.
